subject: Hyperscaler delta validation — hallucination gap triage & sandbox run
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tan <sophie@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: suggested delta validations and hallucination probes

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a concrete proposal so your eng and procurement teams have what they need to validate us vs the hyperscalers you mentioned.

Summary of where Redwood stood out in the demo:
- More predictable P95 on short-chat flows under mixed load (we observed <250ms in our dedicated-sim run).
- Built-in prefix/KV caching reduced token counts by ~20% for multi-turn doc assistants in our probes.
- Private deployment option and explicit KMS integration were differentiators for your security folks.

What we propose as the next validation work (90–120 minute sandbox + 48–72 hour run window):
1) Representative input pack: run your 500-sample "support+kb" pack (attached novacorp-sample-pack.zip) against: Redwood-hosted (baseline), Redwood-quantized (q4_0), HyperscalerA-standard, HyperscalerB-Large.
   - Report per-sample: hallucination flag, factual-consistency score, token usage, P50/P95 latency.
2) Hallucination probe set: a curated 60-prompt set (attached probe_prompts_v1.csv) with: counterfactual fact checks, date-sensitive queries, and instruction-following traps.
3) Regression checks: snapshot outputs and diffs; we’ll run a regression harness and produce a CSV you can ingest.

Success thresholds we recommend for decisioning:
- Hallucination rate (as defined in the probe set) < 3% differential vs HyperscalerA, and absolute < 5% across probes.
- P95 latency under 300ms for single-turn queries in your region.
- Cost: token cost delta and end-to-end token counts reported per 1k tokens.

Logistics / ask of NovaCorp:
- Share a single S3 path or zipped sample (we attached a seed pack).
- Confirm an engineering contact for access (we’ll need an IP allowlist for the sandbox).
- If procurement needs SOC2 / audit artifacts, I’ll CC our security lead in the next message.

I’m happy to run the sandbox this week if you can confirm sample + eng contact. Proposed window: Fri 21 May 09:00–12:00 PT for the live run kick-off.

Thanks — Ir
--
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Sophie Tan <sophie@novacorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: suggested delta validations and hallucination probes

Thanks Irene — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick Qs from my side:

- Can you confirm sample size flexibility? We may want to start with 200 focused cases and scale to 500 if the first tranche looks good.
- Our eng team (engineering@novacorp.com) says IP allowlist is fine but we need a short on-boarding checklist so they can provision access.
- Procurement asked whether you can provide a SOC2 summary and typical SLAs up front — I’ll loop them in on a separate thread but if you can drop a short artifact that helps.

We should be able to join the kick-off on Fri 21 May at 09:00 PT. I’ll include our eng lead on the calendar invite.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Tan
Head of Product, NovaCorp
sophie@novacorp.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: test plan + quick priorities (DEAL-4821)

Irene — good plan. Internal notes / asks before the Fri run:

- We'll prepare two model variants: baseline (fp16) and quantized q4_0. Also include an 8-bit dynamic run if slot available.
- Test matrix: 200 focused probes first (fast turnaround), then expand to 500 if delta < 10% in first tranche.
- Thresholds to present in the report: hallucination delta vs HyperscalerA <= 3% and absolute <5%; P95 < 300ms; token cost delta < 15%.
- I’ll spin up the sandbox with telemetry hooks (trace ids + sample ids) and share the drive link to results.

Marissa — can you prepare the redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-matrix.xlsx and include the exact column headers Sophie asked for (sample_id, prompt, expected_facts, baseline_output, q4_output, hyperscalerA_output, hyperscalerB_output, hallucination_flag, latency_ms, token_count)?

Irene — I’ll also attach our SOC2 summary in the kick-off invite.

– Marcus
Senior Product, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tan <sophie@novacorp.com>, engineering@novacorp.com, procurement@novacorp.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: suggested delta validations and hallucination probes — kick-off confirmed

Hi Sophie / NovaCorp team — great, confirmed for Fri 21 May 09:00 PT. Calendar invite will follow. Attaching the seed artifacts for the run: probe_prompts_v1.csv, novacorp-sample-pack.zip and the test matrix template (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-matrix.xlsx).

Agenda for the 30–45 minute kick-off:
- Quick intro + roles (5 min)
- Walk the test matrix and probe semantics (10 min)
- Sandbox access & telemetry / data handling notes (10 min)
- Immediate next steps and timeline (10 min)

Deliverables we'll provide within 72 hours of kick-off:
- Full result CSV with per-sample outputs across variants.
- Hallucination-rate delta report and a short executive summary for procurement.
- Raw traces and a short how-to for your team to reproduce locally if you want to run additional variants.

If procurement wants the SOC2 summary now, attaching the short PDF in a follow-up (Marcus will drop it in the invite). Looking forward — Ir
